newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt finances wallowing - data.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt finances wallowing - data.

text.p: Australian Finance Department data issued on Friday shows no trend improvement in government finances and no progress towards the government's goals for the current fiscal year.
But government officials pointed to big changes in the pattern of company tax payments as a reason for the slow progress. They expect a catch up as the financial year wears on.
The underlying budget deficit for the 12 months to November was A$13.3 billion, up from A$10.7 billion in October and no improvement on typical results for the past year.
The government attributes the weakness to:
--On the spending side, higher-than-expected social security (not including unemployment benefits) and medical payments to the states under the national health insurance scheme, Medicare.
--On the revenue side, a change in timing of company tax payments.
The deficit for the 12 months to June -- which is recorded as the 1995/96 financial year result -- was A$10.3 billion, which, being lower than all surrounding data, appeared to be an anomally.
By June 1997, eight months away, the deficit is supposed to shrink to A$5.6 billion. Instead it is, at best, going nowhere.
Twelve-month revenue in October was A$121.0 billion, maintaining the improvement that appeared last month, when the figure exceeded A$120 billion.
But spending, at A$128.2 billion, has jumped back to near the record 12-month levels recorded in July and August.

Government finance sources pointed to timing changes as throwing the government finances off schedule. For example, the big social security bill included an extra fortnightly payment in recent months compared with a year before.
Similarly, corporate tax had moved to a new pattern.
Last year, large companies paid 85 percent of their tax liability in the September quarter.
This year, they paid only 25 percent, with the rest to follow regularly through the year.
